Subject: Technical readiness check — Orion Medical private deployment (next steps)

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the team. Below is a concise recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we pull in the solutions team for a site survey. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Recap of requirements (per today’s call):
- Deployment mode: Private (air-gapped) in Orion datacenter; no outbound internet from inference cluster.
- Expected steady-state throughput: 6–12 requests/sec for inference peaks tied to imaging pipeline, burst to ~25rps for batch ingest windows.
- Model profile: two primary models — a 7B-class for metadata extraction and a 13B-class for image annotation.
- Hardware currently available: you mentioned 8x NVIDIA A100 40GB (mixed servers), 150TB SAN behind the cluster.
- Maintenance constraints: quarterly maintenance windows only; software upgrades must be coordinated and can be delivered via encrypted media (no direct download).
- Compliance: audit logs, PKCS11-compatible KMS preferred.

Immediate follow-ups we will action:
1) Solutions to confirm memory/kv-cache strategy for the 13B variant and whether a 40GB A100 can host the required configurations (Dev will confirm memory headroom).
2) Share a lightweight site-survey template and an operations checklist for air-gapped image upgrades. (Attached: redwood-onprem-requirements-v1.pdf and site-survey-template.xlsx)
3) Propose dates for an onsite/remote survey week of Jun 22 to validate rack/cabling and firmware levels.
4) Draft a minimal MOP for offline upgrades (physical media chain-of-custody, verification hashes, rollback plan) and circulate for your review.

Questions we still have for you:
- Is there a preferred lab or staging rack where we can perform a dry-run before the production cutover?
- Who will be the primary IT contact for hardware/firmware (name + phone) for scheduling the survey?

Next steps / Ask of Orion:
- Please confirm availability for a 90-min site survey window between Jun 22–26.
- Share the contact details for the person who will coordinate access and courier acceptance for encrypted media.

I’ll loop in Dev for the technical deep-dive once we have availability.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and answers below after I checked with the ops team.

Confirmed details:
- Hardware: we currently have 8x A100 40GB across two identical 2U servers (4 cards each) and two older 8-card chassis being decommissioned in Q3. The SAN is a Dell/Isilon cluster with ~150TB usable.
- Network: the inference network is on an isolated VLAN; no outgoing NAT allowed. We can provision a temporary staging VLAN for the survey if needed.
- Maintenance windows: typically Friday 0200–0600 local.

Questions / constraints from IT:
1) Upgrade model: We require an auditable offline update process. Any software/images must be signed and checksummed. Transfers will be via encrypted external SSD couriered to our security desk.
2) Licensing/activation: offline license activation is required; we do not allow outbound calls for license verification.
3) Kernel/firmware: we can schedule firmware updates but they require a 2-week lead and an approval ticket.
4) Physical constraints: rack U-space is limited; please confirm total U and power draw (we have 2x 32A circuits per rack).

Technical notes / asks for Redwood:
- Can Redwood support an installer image that can be applied fully offline with a signed manifest and offline activation token?
- What’s your recommended GPU memory footprint for the 13B model to work acceptably on a 40GB A100 (we may need to consider quantized model variants)?
- Provide a short checklist of pre-requisites we can run ahead of the site scheduler to speed the visit.

I’ve attached our current rack layout (rack-layout_v2.pdf) and would prefer Jun 24 (any time) for the survey if your team can do the morning slot.

Thanks,
Maria Galvez
Head of IT Operations — Orion Medical Devices
maria.galvez@orionmed.com | +1 (617) 555-0122

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Technical readiness check — Orion Medical private deployment (next steps)

Quick technical read from my side after reviewing Maria’s notes and their rack layout. TL;DR: feasible with caveats.

Key points:
- Memory/Model fitting: A 40GB A100 can host a quantized 13B variant with 8-bit PTQ or Q4_0 approaches with careful KV-cache management; warm K/V cache to SAN will likely require tuning but we can prototype. For the 7B model, standard float/8-bit quant is fine.
- Offline installer: We can produce a signed installer image plus a separate signed manifest and an offline activation token workflow. That fits their no-outbound constraint — we’ll need to add a one-time activation handshake that can be done via a signed token file.
- Upgrades & rollback: Recommend a two-image strategy on the host (A & B) with a verified hash and immediate fallback; this minimizes risk during offline patching.
- Power/U: need exact rack U per server; their 2x32A per rack sounds OK but we should get server PSU draw with peak load.

Proposed immediate actions for the survey:
1) Confirm exact PSU model and measured power draw from Orion (we can provide a measurement script).
2) Validate node BIOS and driver versions (we’ll send an inventory script to run on a staging node).
3) Prepare offline image package (signed), a verification script, and a MOP draft. I can own the image prep if we get sample hardware details.

I recommend we treat this as Redwood Private (air-gapped) with the following deliverables ahead of the visit: signed installer image, signed manifest, pre-flight inventory script, and the draft MOP. Happy to join the site visit remotely.
